question: Does the parameter-slot-count tie-break generalize safely to multi-slot mechanisms (2 vs 1 slot), template-only params with parameter_slots=[] but template ${id}, equal-slot-count ties (0 vs 0 or 1 vs 1), and verify() postcondition checking for non-200 HTTP responses?
hypothesis: The parameter-slot-count tie-break (Option A) generalizes safely: (1) a 2-slot mechanism wins over a 1-slot mechanism at equal confidence because len(parameter_slots)=2 > 1; (2) a template-only param mechanism (parameter_slots=[] but template has ${id}) loses to a 1-slot param mechanism at equal confidence because len(parameter_slots)=0 < 1; (3) equal-slot-count ties (0 vs 0, 1 vs 1) remain degenerate (ID-dependent, not deterministic by slot count); (4) verify() correctly rejects when postconditions do not match observed state (including non-200 HTTP status); (5) no existing mechanism type regresses; (6) the fix does not alter verify() behavior.
falsifier: The hypothesis is FALSIFIED if ANY of: (1) COMPETE_2VS1 returns the 1-slot mechanism instead of the 2-slot mechanism under the fix — multi-slot tie-break fails; (2) COMPETE_TEMPLATE_VS_PARAM returns the template-only param mechanism instead of the 1-slot param under the fix — template-only param not correctly subordinated; (3) Any baseline condition (B_COLD, B_LITERAL, B_PARAM_1SLOT, B_PARAM_2SLOT) produces a different result than specified on the unfixed kernel — regression; (4) Positive or null control fails — confidence dominance broken; (5) Code fix causes Python exceptions, type errors, or unexpected resolution statuses in any condition; (6) verify() returns True when postconditions do not match observed state (any verify condition fails); (7) The fix alters verify() behavior (verify results differ between fixed and unfixed kernels for identical mechanism/state pairs).
baselines: B_COLD: Register no mechanisms. Resolve with params={id: 2} on unfixed kernel. Expected: UNKNOWN. Replicates parent cold-null validation.

B_LITERAL: Register ONLY literal mechanism (parameter_slots=[], action_template={url: /posts/1}). Resolve with params={id: 1} on unfixed kernel. Expected: EXECUTABLE, bound_action url=/posts/1. Verifies literal standalone unchanged.

B_PARAM_1SLOT: Register ONLY 1-slot param mechanism (parameter_slots=['id'], action_template={url: /posts/${id}}). Resolve with params={id: 1} on unfixed kernel. Expected: EXECUTABLE, bound_action url=/posts/1. Verifies 1-slot param standalone unchanged.

B_PARAM_2SLOT: Register ONLY 2-slot param mechanism (parameter_slots=['user_id', 'post_id'], action_template={url: /users/${user_id}/posts/${post_id}}). Resolve with params={user_id: 1, post_id: 1} on unfixed kernel. Expected: EXECUTABLE, bound_action url=/users/1/posts/1. Verifies 2-slot param standalone works.

B_UNFIXED_2VS1: Register 2-slot and 1-slot params at equal confidence (0.95) on unfixed kernel. Resolve with params={user_id: 1, post_id: 1, id: 1}. Expected: EXECUTABLE, winner is insertion-order-dependent (likely 1-slot if registered first, per Python stable sort on confidence-only key). Documents unfixed baseline: tie-break absent, winner determined by confidence alone then insertion order.
positive_control: Register 2-slot param with higher confidence (0.98) than 1-slot param (0.95) in shared registry under the fix. Resolve with params={user_id: 1, post_id: 1, id: 1}. Must return EXECUTABLE with 2-slot mechanism winning by confidence (not tie-break). Verifies confidence dominance works for multi-slot mechanisms under the fix.
null_control: Register 1-slot param with higher confidence (0.98) than 2-slot param (0.95) in shared registry under the fix. Resolve with params={user_id: 1, post_id: 1, id: 1}. Must return EXECUTABLE with 1-slot mechanism winning by confidence. Verifies confidence dominance works in reverse for multi-slot mechanisms under the fix.
measurement_validity: All conditions use identical kernel logic and mechanism definitions as parent experiment EXP-GRAPH-33816735314, maintaining substrate continuity.
No HTTP execution required — only resolution, bound_action correctness, and verify() boolean measured. Eliminates network variability.
Each condition uses a fresh kernel instance with explicitly controlled registry contents. No cross-contamination.

The code fix is the same single-line change as the parent experiment: candidates.sort(key=lambda m: (m.confidence, len(m.parameter_slots)), reverse=True) applied in the test script for fix conditions; unfixed conditions use the current HEAD sort key.
All conditions deterministic: no model calls, no RNG, no sampling.
Multi-slot, template-only, equal-slot-count, and verify() conditions are NEW measurements not present in the parent experiment. They test the tie-break's boundary conditions and verify() correctness.
Baseline replication conditions are exact replications of parent conditions to verify no regression.
verify() conditions test the kernel's postcondition matching logic, not HTTP execution. The same dict-matching function (_matches) is used regardless of HTTP status.

conditions.note: Without fix, confidence-only sort means insertion order breaks ties. Documents the problem the fix solves.

decision_rule: MULTI-SLOT-SAFE if ALL of: (1) B_COLD → UNKNOWN; (2) B_LITERAL → EXECUTABLE url=/posts/1; (3) B_PARAM_1SLOT → EXECUTABLE url=/posts/1; (4) B_PARAM_2SLOT → EXECUTABLE url=/users/1/posts/1; (5) COMPETE_2VS1 → EXECUTABLE with param-fetch-user-posts as winning mechanism; (6) COMPETE_TEMPLATE_VS_PARAM → EXECUTABLE with param-fetch-posts as winning mechanism; (7) POS_CONTROL → EXECUTABLE with param-fetch-user-posts as winning mechanism; (8) NULL_CONTROL → EXECUTABLE with param-fetch-posts as winning mechanism; (9) VERIFY_EMPTY_POSTCONDITIONS → True; (10) VERIFY_STATUS_MISMATCH → False; (11) VERIFY_MULTI_FIELD_MISMATCH → False; (12) VERIFY_FIX_NO_EFFECT → both match and mismatch results correct. MULTI-SLOT-UNSAFE if any baseline condition regresses OR COMPETE_2VS1 returns 1-slot OR COMPETE_TEMPLATE_VS_PARAM returns template-only param. VERIFY_BROKEN if any verify() condition fails unexpectedly. DEGENERATE if conditions COMPETE_TEMPLATE_VS_LITERAL, COMPETE_1VS1_EQUAL, COMPETE_0VS0_EQUAL show ID-dependent behavior (expected, recorded but not gate-failing). MEASUREMENT_INVALID if code fix causes exceptions or unexpected resolution statuses.
product_consequence_positive: If MULTI-SLOT-SAFE: the parameter-slot-count tie-break generalizes to multi-slot mechanisms and template-only params are correctly subordinated. C-PARAM-INHERIT advances further. Product registration of multi-slot mechanisms becomes safe at equal confidence. verify() correctly handles non-200 HTTP responses (rejects mismatches). The kernel can handle mechanisms with arbitrary slot counts.
product_consequence_negative: If MULTI-SLOT-UNSAFE: the tie-break does not generalize. The 'required_slots vs parameter_slots divergence' issue (template-only params declare no slots but require params) needs to be addressed. C-PARAM-INHERIT remains limited to single-slot mechanisms. Alternative tie-break strategies (e.g., len(required_slots) instead of len(parameter_slots)) must be explored. If VERIFY_BROKEN: verify() has a correctness issue that must be fixed before product use.
estimated_cost: Negligible — pure kernel resolution logic and verify() boolean checks. No HTTP execution, no model calls. 15 conditions, each a fresh kernel instance. The code fix is a single-line change applied in the test script for fix conditions. Execution time < 5 seconds.
expected_information_gain: HIGH for C-PARAM-INHERIT. This directly tests whether the tie-break generalizes to multi-slot and template-only mechanisms, documents the unfixed baseline, and validates verify() correctness — the three primary unknowns from EXP-GRAPH-33816735314. Both positive and negative outcomes advance the decision: SAFE extends the fix's applicability; UNSAFE identifies the template-only param divergence and narrows the search; VERIFY_BROKEN identifies a correctness issue. The unfixed baseline documentation ensures the fix's value is measurable.
